title: Endpoint operationalization PRD: converged call surface for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank + launch checklist
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: This PRD defines the requirements, acceptance criteria, and launch checklist for the unified API call surface that exposes chat, completion, embeddings, and rerank capabilities. Goal: ship a predictable, observable, and secure hosted surface that lets customers switch between model variants with consistent contracts and clear operational SLAs. This doc focuses on the production acceptance gates (functional, perf, security, observability), staged rollout plan, and post-launch monitoring obligations.
objectives: 1) Provide a single, documented REST surface that supports chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank with consistent authentication, error semantics, and telemetry. 2) Ensure P50/P95 latency and cost guidance per model tier and enforceable SLOs. 3) Enable safe canary and gradual rollout controls with automatic fallback to tiered model variants. 4) Ship a checklist that allows Support/EngOps to validate readiness and operate the surface post-launch.
scope_inclusions:
- Chat (multi-turn state + function/tool calling)
- Completions (single-shot and streaming)
- Embeddings (batched and single input)
- Rerank service (k-best scoring + normalized scores)
- Auth and quotas compatible with existing hosted API
- Token-level billing and breakdowns in telemetry
- Basic structured output and deterministic contract for JSON outputs
scope_exclusions:
- Multi-modal inputs (images/audio) for this rollout
- Dedicated customer-managed private control plane features
- Advanced RBAC and org-level hierarchy beyond standard api-key scopes
- Auto-quantization recommendation tooling (deferred to Optimize)
requirements:
1) API contract: clear request/response schemas for each surface (examples + edge cases)
2) Error model: documented set of retryable vs non-retryable errors and HTTP codes
3) Latency SLOs: P50/P95 targets by model tier (see metrics)
4) Throughput: embeddings batch throughput baseline and max request size limits
5) Cost/usage telemetry: per-request token counts, model variant, route, and cost estimate
6) Rollout controls: canary percentage, region targeting, and automatic fallback policies
7) Security: data encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs
8) Observability: per-route dashboards, request tracing, and anomaly alerts tied to guardrails
9) Tests: end-to-end integration tests, performance harnesses, and regression suites for quality
success_metrics:
- Functional correctness: 0 major contract regressions in validation suite
- Latency: P50 < 60ms for small sequence completion on tier-1 models; P95 < 250ms (hosted EU/NA)
- Embeddings throughput: 1000 single-item requests/sec per pool baseline in synthetic harness
- Rerank precision: mean normalized score correlation >= 0.85 vs baseline reranker on test sets
- Error budget: <1% 5xxs in first 72h and <0.5% thereafter
- Adoption: 50+ unique dev tokens using new surface in first 30 days
acceptance_criteria:
Functional:
- All API routes return responses consistent with contract for positive and negative cases
- Streaming paths close streams reliably under network churn tests
Performance:
- Perf harness demonstrates target P50/P95 per model tier across supported regions
- Batching and KV cache do not regress tail latency by >10% at target QPS
Security & Compliance:
- KMS integration validated with at least one customer config in staging
- Audit logs contain request_id, user_id, model_variant, and decision/fallback reason
Observability:
- Dashboards surface per-route latency, QPS, token cost, and error breakdowns
- Health check probe indicates readiness and exposes eviction/backpressure signals
Operational:
- Canary rollout automation supports 0%, 1%, 5%, 25%, 100% stages with automated rollback on predefined triggers
- Runbook exists and has been exercised in a simulated failover
test_plan:
- Integration: Run full request/response regression across chat/completion/embeddings/rerank with seeded prompts and golden outputs
- Load: Synthetic load against staging to validate autoscaling behavior, KV cache hit rates, and batching efficiency
- Chaos: Simulate region failover, slow GPUs, and degraded network to validate fallbacks and routing policies
- Security: Pen-test / dependency scanning and KMS key rotation scenario verification
- Quality: Eval harness comparing generation quality across model variants and ensuring no regression in intent recall
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: Internal dogfood only (Engineering + SE) - duration 3 days
Phase 1: Invite-only beta (selected customers and partners) - duration 7 days
Phase 2: Wider canary (1% -> 5% -> 25%) over 7 days with automated rollback gates
Phase 3: General availability if no critical regressions and SLOs met for 72h
Fallback policy: if error budget exceeds threshold or P95 regresses >20% for 3 consecutive evaluation windows, automatically route to fallback variant and pause percentage increase
launch_checklist:
Pre-launch:
- [ ] API spec published and integrated into SDKs
- [ ] Integration tests passing in staging and preprod
- [ ] Perf harness results uploaded to dashboard and signed off by Reliability
- [ ] Security review completed and any open findings either mitigated or accepted
- [ ] Runbook and escalation matrix published to Support
- [ ] Billing/usage lineage tied to token meters and cost breakdown verified
Launch window:
- [ ] Canary policy enabled and first 1% traffic observed
- [ ] Live telemetry (latency, error, cost) monitored by on-call SRE and PM
- [ ] Rollback knobs tested and reachable within 5 minutes
Post-launch (first 72h):
- [ ] Daily sync between PM/Eng/SRE and Support for first 3 days
- [ ] Confirm error budget <1% and P95 within target for each region
- [ ] Customer feedback channel monitored and initial tickets triaged
risks_mitigation:
- Risk: KV cache or batching causes tail latency regressions. Mitigation: include fallback path that disables batching for affected model variant and alerting to SRE.
- Risk: Rerank score drift after upstream model change. Mitigation: maintain eval set with periodic regression checks and block rollout if correlation drops below threshold.
- Risk: Billing mismatch for streaming tokens. Mitigation: reconcile token counting in staging with production billing team and include telemetry tag exposing token accounting per SDK version.
- Risk: Canary insufficient coverage for long-tail prompts. Mitigation: seed canary with production-like traffic replay and invite known customers representing varied workloads.
notes:
- Decision: initial GA will not support multi-modal inputs; roadmap item for Q3.
- Follow-up: coordinate with Optimize for model quantization guidance before expanding to lower-cost tiers.
- Observability ask: add token cost heatmap to per-route dashboards before GA.
